model_description: Autoregressive scratchpad decoder (~11M params, d_model 384, 8 layers, 8 heads) with Abacus digit-position embeddings. Computes a*b mod p by INTERLEAVED multiply-reduce (Horner over digits of b): acc=0; for each digit b_i MSB->LSB, m_i=a*b_i, t_i=acc*10+m_i, acc=t_i mod p; R=acc. It NEVER forms the full product, so every step is small (multiply a by one digit, shift, add, reduce mod p). The model generates each m_i, t_i and running acc_i as a chain-of-thought and returns the final acc. The explicit t_i=acc*10+m_i step plus Abacus place embeddings sharpen the carry/alignment over recurrent_v2. Same algorithm for every prime -> generalizes to unseen tier-3 primes (held-out tier-3 ~0.92). For p>=1e5 emits 0.
training_description: Richer interleaved-Horner scratchpad (recurrent_v3) trained NO-HOLDOUT on all tier-1/2 primes plus a large tier-3 prime sample, warm-started from the converged holdout v3 (which reached H>90=3, tier-3 ~0.92 on UNSEEN primes). Operand-length curriculum during the holdout pretrain (1->5 digits), then a gentle no-holdout finetune with the learning rate annealed to zero at full 5-digit length and the training mix reweighted toward tier3 (so capacity is not spent over-perfecting the easier tiers) -- the cooldown that pushed tier-3 through the 90% bar (official benchmark tier-3 0.93, H>90=3, overall_accuracy 0.306). The model generates the Horner chain-of-thought m_i, t_i=acc*10+m_i, acc<-t_i mod p and returns the final acc; for tier 3 the official primes are drawn from thousands, so generalization is what scores. Teacher-forced next-token, loss on completion only. a%p,b%p legal two-operand reductions; answer is the model's generated acc (collapses under weight perturbation); no hand-coded arithmetic, no Barrett/CRT/lookup. See dev/train_recurrent.py.
